option_description: Lowest TLS/SSL protocol version the server will negotiate (nginx ssl_protocols / Apache SSLProtocol). A secure posture offers only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3; offering SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1 permits a downgrade attack.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Weak TLS termination" — fires when min_tls_version is the deprecated value tls1_0_or_tls1_1_or_sslv3_accepted, letting an on-path attacker force a downgrade to a broken protocol (POODLE/BEAST) and decrypt session traffic (T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the negotiated TLS versions from the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; (secure) vs a line including TLSv1 or TLSv1.1 (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan the listener with testssl.sh to see which protocol versions actually negotiate.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS 1.2/1.3 offered; SSLv2/SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1 reported as 'not offered' (secure) or 'offered (NOT ok)' (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: testssl.sh — Testing TLS/SSL encryption anywhere on any port

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate offered protocols/ciphers on the wire with nmap.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 sections present; no TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 sections and no ciphers graded D/F

option_description: Interpreted assertion that the negotiated cipher suites exclude weak/legacy ciphers (RC4, DES/3DES, EXPORT, NULL, MD5, non-PFS) and offer only forward-secret AEAD suites (ECDHE+GCM/ChaCha20, Mozilla Intermediate/Modern). Set via nginx ssl_ciphers / Apache SSLCipherSuite.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Weak TLS termination" — fires when strong_cipher_suite_enforced is false (weak ciphers not disabled), enabling weak-crypto MITM / decryption of intercepted traffic (T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured cipher list and preference flag from the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mozilla-generated ssl_ciphers line; ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off for TLS1.3-only / on for intermediate

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan which ciphers actually negotiate per protocol with testssl.sh.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only forward-secret AEAD ciphers offered; no RC4/3DES/EXPORT/NULL flagged
how_to_obtain.source: Mozilla Server Side TLS — Recommended Configurations

option_description: Whether HTTP Strict-Transport-Security is served with an effective policy (max-age >= 2 years, includeSubDomains), forcing HTTPS and defeating SSL-strip/downgrade (RFC 6797).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Weak TLS termination" — fires when hsts_enabled is false (HSTS absent or ineffective), so an on-path attacker can strip TLS on the first request and downgrade the client to plaintext (T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the HSTS response header served over HTTPS.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains (secure) vs no such header (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the HSTS add_header directive is present in the running config with an effective max-age.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains" always;
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_http_headers_module — add_header for security headers

option_description: Interpreted assertion that the served certificate is valid: CA-issued (not self-signed for public), unexpired, full chain, strong key (>=2048-bit RSA / 256-bit ECDSA) and SHA-256+ signature.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Weak TLS termination" — fires when server_certificate_validated is false (expired/self-signed/weak-key cert), undermining endpoint authentication and enabling adversary-in-the-middle (T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Fetch the served certificate and inspect its dates, subject and issuer.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect target:443 -servername target </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates -subject -issuer
how_to_obtain.expected_output: notAfter in future; issuer is a trusted CA; subject matches host
how_to_obtain.source: testssl.sh — Testing TLS/SSL encryption anywhere on any port

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run a full TLS scan to grade certificate chain, key strength and signature algorithm.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Certificate section: trusted chain, key >=2048-bit RSA / 256-bit ECDSA, SHA-256+ signature, not expired
how_to_obtain.source: testssl.sh — Testing TLS/SSL encryption anywhere on any port

option_description: True when the server software (nginx/Apache/etc.) is running a current stable patched release within the patch SLA, not a version affected by an open RCE/DoS advisory.
security_impact: Trigger of "Unpatched server-software CVE (RCE / DoS)" — fires when software_version_patched is false, meaning the running version is behind a known advisory (e.g. CVE-2024-24990 HTTP/3 use-after-free, CVE-2025-23419 TLS session-reuse, CVE-2023-44487 HTTP/2 Rapid Reset) directly exploitable on an internet-facing server (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running server version string and compare against the vendor advisory page for known-fixed releases.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: version string compared against the vendor advisory page for known-fixed releases

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the running release sits past the fixed version for every open advisory affecting the product, and that the deployment meets the organization's patch SLA.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No open RCE/DoS advisory applies to the running build; patch SLA met
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application

option_description: Number of days since the server software was last patched/updated. A long-unpatched internet-facing server accumulates exposure to newly-disclosed advisories.
security_impact: Secondary OR-trigger of "Unpatched server-software CVE (RCE / DoS)" — fires above the patch-SLA threshold (30 days), reinforcing patch-currency for T1190 exposure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Compare the package/build install timestamp against today and report elapsed days.
how_to_obtain.command: dpkg -l nginx 2>/dev/null; rpm -qi nginx 2>/dev/null | grep -i 'install date'; stat -c '%y' $(command -v nginx)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Install/build date; elapsed days computed against today (should be within the 30-day patch SLA)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check the package manager log for the most recent upgrade of the web-server package.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -i nginx /var/log/dpkg.log /var/log/apt/history.log 2>/dev/null | tail; grep -i nginx /var/log/yum.log /var/log/dnf.rpm.log 2>/dev/null | tail
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Most recent upgrade/install entry for the web-server package; date used to compute elapsed days

option_description: True when the experimental HTTP/3 (QUIC) listener is enabled (nginx ngx_http_v3). The secure value is false (QUIC off unless required) because enabling it widens the attack surface.
security_impact: Insecure-widening OR-trigger of "Unpatched server-software CVE (RCE / DoS)" — fires on is_true, since the experimental QUIC listener was the vector for CVE-2024-24990 (use-after-free worker crash) and expands the exploitable surface (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether an HTTP/3 QUIC listener is configured in the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No match (HTTP/3 off = secure) vs a 'listen ... quic' or 'http3 on' line (enabled = insecure-widening)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the host for an advertised HTTP/3 endpoint over UDP/443.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No HTTP/3 service responding (secure) vs an HTTP/3 alt-svc / successful --http3 response (enabled)

option_description: True when version/banner disclosure is suppressed — nginx server_tokens off, Apache ServerTokens Prod + ServerSignature Off — so the Server header and error pages do not leak the exact product version. nginx/Apache default to disclosing it.
security_impact: An is_false-firing OR-trigger of BOTH "Unpatched server-software CVE (RCE / DoS)" and "Server hardening gaps & info disclosure" — when false, exact version tokens fingerprint the stack, easing targeted CVE selection (T1592.002) and accelerating T1190 exploitation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the server_tokens directive in the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: server_tokens off; (secure) vs on/absent — default is on (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_http_core_module — banner, methods, body/header limits

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Server response header on the wire.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: server: nginx (no version) or removed entirely (secure) vs server: nginx/1.30.0 (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Apache, check the ServerTokens / ServerSignature directives.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ServerTokens Prod and ServerSignature Off (secure); default Full/On (insecure)

option_description: Whether the web server worker processes run as a dedicated unprivileged user (e.g. nginx/www-data) rather than root. Set via the nginx 'user' directive; the master binds privileged ports then drops privilege.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Web-shell foothold via writable webroot / excessive privilege" — fires when worker_process_runs_unprivileged is false, since root-running workers mean a worker compromise yields root and any dropped web shell executes with full privilege (T1505.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured worker user from the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: user nginx; (non-root)
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_core_module — worker process privilege (user directive)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the running worker processes are not owned by root.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: worker rows owned by www-data/nginx, not root (secure)
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_core_module — worker process privilege (user directive)

option_description: Whether the webroot/code directories are writable by the serving (worker) user. The INSECURE value is true; least privilege (AC-6) requires the serving user to have read-only access to the served document root.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Web-shell foothold via writable webroot / excessive privilege" — fires when webroot_writable_by_server_user is true, since write+serve on the same path lets an attacker drop and then execute a server-side script (T1505.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: List webroot ownership/permissions and search for files writable by the serving user.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no world/group-writable files; serving user lacks write (secure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the worker user specifically cannot write the document root.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no rows (serving user cannot write the served document root = secure)

option_description: True when dangerous/unused HTTP write methods are disabled and only needed verbs are exposed (GET/HEAD/POST as needed; TraceEnable Off; no PUT/DELETE/WebDAV PROPFIND/MKCOL unless required).
security_impact: OR-trigger of BOTH "Web-shell foothold via writable webroot / excessive privilege" and "Server hardening gaps & info disclosure" — fires when http_method_allow_list_enforced is false, since an enabled PUT/WebDAV turns a write primitive into a web-shell upload path (T1505.003) and TRACE enables cross-site tracing / method fingerprinting (T1592.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Allow header advertised by an OPTIONS request.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Allow: GET, HEAD, POST only (secure) vs includes PUT/DELETE/TRACE/PROPFIND (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_http_core_module — banner, methods, body/header limits

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe whether TRACE is enabled (cross-site tracing).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 405 Method Not Allowed / 501 (secure) vs 200 echoing the request (insecure — TRACE enabled)

option_description: True when automatic directory listing is disabled — nginx has no 'autoindex on;' (off is default), Apache uses 'Options -Indexes'. When enabled, a directory without an index file returns an 'Index of /' page exposing the full file tree.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Server hardening gaps & info disclosure" — fires when directory_autoindex_disabled is false (autoindex on / Options Indexes), leaking the file layout (backups, configs, source) for targeted retrieval (T1083).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for any autoindex on; directives in the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no autoindex on; lines (off is default = secure); any 'autoindex on;' is insecure

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request a directory with no index file and look for a generated listing.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no 'Index of /' page returned (secure) vs an HTML directory listing (insecure)

option_description: True when shipped default/sample/welcome files and demo pages are removed from the webroot. Vendor-default content fingerprints the product and version and may itself carry known vulnerabilities.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Server hardening gaps & info disclosure" — fires when sample_apps_and_default_content_removed is false, since default index/sample/test content aids stack enumeration (T1592.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe for common vendor default pages on the served host.
how_to_obtain.command: for p in / /index.nginx-debian.html /icons/ /manual/ /test.php /info.php; do echo -n "$p "; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://target$p; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 404 for vendor default/sample paths (removed = secure) vs 200 returning the shipped default/sample content (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the served document root for shipped default index pages, sample apps and demo/test content.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No vendor default/sample/demo files present in the served document root

option_description: True when built-in status/admin endpoints (nginx stub_status, Apache mod_status server-status, /admin) are IP-restricted (allow 127.0.0.1; deny all;) or disabled, rather than reachable from the internet.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Server hardening gaps & info disclosure" — fires when status_endpoints_access_restricted is false, since publicly-reachable /server-status / /nginx_status leak internal metrics, connections, request paths and config for reconnaissance (T1595.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request the status endpoints from an external network and read the HTTP code.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 403/404 from public source (secure) vs 200 with status output (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the status locations are gated by an access rule in the running config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: status/admin locations carry allow 127.0.0.1; deny all; (or auth) — not openly reachable

option_description: Attested true when the server denies direct access to VCS metadata and dotfiles under webroot (e.g. nginx 'location ~ /\.(git|svn|env) { deny all; }') OR those files are kept out of the served document root.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Sensitive-file / path exposure" — fires when dotfiles_and_vcs_metadata_blocked is false (e.g. GET /.git/config or /.env returns 200 with contents), leaking source and secrets (T1083).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe common dotfile / VCS-metadata paths and read the HTTP codes.
how_to_obtain.command: for p in /.git/config /.env /.svn/entries; do echo -n "$p "; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://target$p; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 403/404 for every probe (secure) vs 200 returning file contents (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a deny rule for dotfiles/VCS metadata exists in the running config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A location block denying ^/\.(git|svn|env) (secure), or files confirmed absent from webroot

option_description: Attested true when editor swap/backup and database/dump files (*.bak, *.old, *.swp, *.sql, config.php~) are denied by server rules OR absent from the served document root.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Sensitive-file / path exposure" — fires when backup_and_swap_files_excluded_from_webroot is false (e.g. GET /backup.sql or /config.php.bak returns 200), leaking source/credentials (T1083).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe common backup/swap filenames and read the HTTP codes.
how_to_obtain.command: for p in /backup.sql /config.php.bak /index.php~ /database.old; do echo -n "$p "; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://target$p; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 403/404 for every probe (secure) vs 200 returning file contents (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a deny rule for backup/swap extensions exists in the running config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A location block denying \.(bak|old|swp|sql)$ (secure), or such files confirmed absent from webroot

option_description: Attested true when the server normalizes and rejects path-traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e, encoded null/dot-segment tricks) so files outside the intended served subtree cannot be reached via crafted URLs.
security_impact: Secondary OR-trigger of "Sensitive-file / path exposure" — fires when path_traversal_protection_enabled is false, since traversal can reach the same VCS metadata / env / backup files even when direct dotfile deny rules exist (T1083).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send crafted traversal URLs and confirm they are normalized/rejected rather than serving files outside the subtree.
how_to_obtain.command: for p in /../../etc/passwd /%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fetc%2fpasswd /..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd; do echo -n "$p "; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://target$p; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 400/403/404 for every probe (normalized/rejected = secure) vs 200 returning a file outside the served subtree (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review alias/root/location handling for unsafe trailing-slash alias patterns that re-enable traversal, and confirm URI normalization is on.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No misconfigured alias allowing dot-segment escape; server normalizes encoded dot-segments before mapping to filesystem

option_description: True when the server sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on responses (including error responses via the 'always' flag), preventing browser MIME-type sniffing.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Missing security response headers" — fires when x_content_type_options_nosniff_set is false, allowing MIME-sniffing-based content interpretation attacks.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the X-Content-Type-Options header on the wire.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: x-content-type-options: nosniff present (secure) vs absent (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the add_header directive is present with the 'always' flag so it applies to error responses.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff always; (applies to error responses too)
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_http_headers_module — add_header for security headers

option_description: True when framing is restricted to defeat clickjacking — either X-Frame-Options: deny/sameorigin or a CSP frame-ancestors directive scoping who may embed the content.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Missing security response headers" — fires when frame_ancestors_restricted is false (no anti-framing control), permitting clickjacking.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for an anti-framing header on the wire.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: X-Frame-Options deny/sameorigin or a CSP frame-ancestors directive present (secure) vs neither (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the framing-control add_header is present in the running config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: add_header X-Frame-Options DENY always; or a CSP with frame-ancestors set
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_http_headers_module — add_header for security headers

option_description: True when the server emits a Referrer-Policy header (e.g. no-referrer or strict-origin-when-cross-origin) limiting referrer leakage to third parties.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Missing security response headers" — fires when referrer_policy_set is false, so the default leaky referrer behavior exposes URLs/paths to third parties.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the Referrer-Policy header on the wire.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: referrer-policy with a restrictive value (no-referrer / strict-origin-when-cross-origin) present (secure) vs absent (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the Referrer-Policy add_header is present in the running config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_http_headers_module — add_header for security headers

option_description: Interpreted from nginx client_max_body_size / Apache LimitRequestBody. True when an explicit bounded request-body size limit is configured; false when bodies are unbounded (client_max_body_size 0) or sized so large that memory/disk can be exhausted.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Request-handling denial of service" — fires when request_body_size_capped is false (unbounded), enabling memory/disk exhaustion via oversized uploads or slow-POST (T1499.004).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured request-body limit from the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: a bounded value (e.g. 10m). default is 1m; '0' means unlimited (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_http_core_module — banner, methods, body/header limits

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Apache, check the LimitRequestBody directive.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An explicit bounded LimitRequestBody value (secure) vs 0/absent (unbounded = insecure)

option_description: Interpreted from nginx client_body_timeout / client_header_timeout / keepalive_timeout (or Apache RequestReadTimeout). True when timeouts are tightened for internet exposure so a slow client cannot hold worker/connection slots open.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Request-handling denial of service" — fires when slowloris_timeouts_configured is false (slack defaults 60s/60s/75s), the primary enabler of Slowloris / slow-POST connection-exhaustion DoS (T1499.004).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the client/keepalive timeouts from the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: tightened values; defaults are 60s/60s/75s (acceptable but high for internet-facing)
how_to_obtain.source: nginx ngx_http_core_module — banner, methods, body/header limits

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Apache, check the mod_reqtimeout RequestReadTimeout directive.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RequestReadTimeout with tightened header/body bounds (secure) vs absent (slowloris-exposed)

option_description: Interpreted from nginx limit_req_zone+limit_req / limit_conn (or Apache mod_ratelimit / mod_qos). True when per-IP request-rate and/or concurrent-connection limits are applied to internet-facing endpoints.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Request-handling denial of service" — fires when request_rate_limiting_enabled is false, leaving public endpoints open to volumetric L7 floods and HTTP/2 Rapid Reset stream-reset abuse (CVE-2023-44487; T1499.004).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for rate/connection-limiting directives in the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: limit_req_zone and limit_req directives present on login/API paths

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Apache, check for mod_qos / mod_ratelimit configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: mod_qos per-IP connection limits or mod_ratelimit applied to public endpoints (secure) vs none (insecure)

option_description: Whether the server enforces a single unambiguous request-framing interpretation consistent with its upstream — rejecting requests presenting both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding, or relying on a deterministic CL/TE precedence shared with the front-end.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "HTTP request smuggling / desync" — fires when request_framing_normalized_front_back is false, since CL/TE disagreement between this server and an upstream proxy enables request smuggling/desync (cache poisoning, auth bypass, request hijacking; T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run a smuggling test tool against the endpoint to detect framing desync.
how_to_obtain.command: Use a smuggling test tool (e.g. Burp HTTP Request Smuggler / smuggler.py) against the endpoint
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no CL.TE / TE.CL / TE.TE desync detected (secure)
how_to_obtain.source: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the server and its upstream share a deterministic CL/TE precedence and that CL+TE requests are rejected rather than forwarded.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Single consistent framing interpretation; conflicting CL+TE requests rejected
how_to_obtain.source: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn

option_description: Whether the server rejects (rather than normalizes or forwards) requests with conflicting or duplicate length-determining headers (duplicate Content-Length, CL+TE together, or malformed chunked framing).
security_impact: OR-trigger of "HTTP request smuggling / desync" — fires when ambiguous_length_headers_rejected is false, letting an attacker craft a request that this server and the upstream parse differently to smuggle a hidden request past front-end controls (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send requests with duplicate Content-Length, CL+TE together, and malformed chunked framing and observe the response.
how_to_obtain.command: Use a smuggling test tool (e.g. Burp HTTP Request Smuggler / smuggler.py) against the endpoint
how_to_obtain.expected_output: server rejects ambiguous requests with 4xx (secure) vs normalizes/forwards them (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the server's framing-rejection posture (duplicate CL, CL+TE, malformed chunked) rejects rather than normalizes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Ambiguous length-header requests are rejected, not silently normalized
how_to_obtain.source: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn

option_description: Whether the server avoids unsafe HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.1 downgrade translation to the upstream that re-introduces CL/TE ambiguity (H2.CL / H2.TE desync). Secure value is true (downgrade hardened or end-to-end HTTP/2 with validated framing).
security_impact: OR-trigger of "HTTP request smuggling / desync" — fires when http2_downgrade_desync_mitigated is false, since rewriting front-end HTTP/2 framing into ambiguous HTTP/1.1 framing the backend mis-parses enables smuggling (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run an H2.CL/H2.TE downgrade-desync test against the endpoint.
how_to_obtain.command: Use a smuggling test tool (e.g. Burp HTTP Request Smuggler / smuggler.py) with HTTP/2 downgrade tests against the endpoint
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no H2.CL / H2.TE downgrade desync detected (secure)
how_to_obtain.source: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the proxy's HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.1 translation configuration; confirm framing is re-validated on downgrade or end-to-end HTTP/2 is used.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Downgrade translation re-validates framing, or end-to-end HTTP/2 with validated framing is in use
how_to_obtain.source: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn

option_description: Whether the server tolerates obfuscated or obsolete Transfer-Encoding tokens (whitespace tricks, duplicate TE headers, 'Transfer-Encoding: identity') instead of strictly normalizing or rejecting them. Secure value is false.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "HTTP request smuggling / desync" — fires when obsolete_transfer_encoding_tolerated is true, since TE.TE desync becomes possible where this server and the upstream disagree on which TE header is authoritative (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send obfuscated/duplicate Transfer-Encoding tokens and observe whether they are rejected.
how_to_obtain.command: Use a smuggling test tool (e.g. Burp HTTP Request Smuggler / smuggler.py) with TE.TE obfuscation tests against the endpoint
how_to_obtain.expected_output: server rejects obfuscated/duplicate TE tokens (secure = tolerated:false) vs tolerates/forwards them (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the server strictly normalizes or rejects whitespace-prefixed TE, duplicate TE and TE: identity rather than forwarding them.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Obsolete/obfuscated Transfer-Encoding requests are rejected, not tolerated
how_to_obtain.source: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn

option_description: Whether the running server version is affected by a known open request-smuggling/desync advisory (e.g. nginx CVE-2019-20372 error_page internal-redirect request smuggling). Secure value is false (past the fixed release).
security_impact: OR-trigger of "HTTP request smuggling / desync" — fires when affected_by_published_smuggling_cve is true, since the framing weakness is exploitable regardless of other hardening (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running server version and compare against vendor desync/smuggling advisories.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: version compared against e.g. nginx CVE-2019-20372 fixed release; build confirmed past the relevant fix (secure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the running build is past the fixed release for known desync CVEs and that error_page internal redirects are not exploitable.
how_to_obtain.command: Confirm server version is past known smuggling/HTTP-2 CVE fixes (e.g. nginx CVE-2019-20372) and that error_page internal redirects are not exploitable
how_to_obtain.expected_output: version >= fixed release for known desync CVEs

option_description: Whether the web server has both access logging and error logging enabled (e.g. nginx access_log/error_log set to real paths, not 'off').
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Inadequate access/error logging" — fires when access_logging_enabled is false, so exploitation attempts and post-compromise activity go unrecorded (hindering detection of T1190 and concealing T1070 log tampering).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the access/error log directives from the running nginx config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: access_log and error_log paths set (not 'off'); ideally piped/forwarded

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Apache, confirm CustomLog and ErrorLog are configured.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CustomLog and ErrorLog set to real paths (secure) vs disabled/absent (insecure)

option_description: Whether access/error logs are forwarded to a central logging system / SIEM (syslog shipping, log agent) rather than kept local-only.
security_impact: OR-trigger of "Inadequate access/error logging" — fires when external_siem_forwarding_enabled is false, since logs that live only on the host can be cleared by an attacker (T1070), crippling detection and forensics.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether logs are piped/forwarded off-host in the web-server logging config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: access_log/error_log piped to a forwarder, or paths picked up by a shipping agent (not local-only)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a log shipper/agent (rsyslog/syslog, Fluent Bit, Vector, etc.) forwards the access/error logs off-host to a central SIEM, and verify arrival in the SIEM.
how_to_obtain.command: systemctl status rsyslog fluent-bit vector 2>/dev/null; grep -RiE 'nginx|access.log|error.log' /etc/rsyslog.d /etc/fluent-bit /etc/vector 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An active shipper with the web-server log paths in its inputs; corresponding events visible in the SIEM (secure) vs no forwarding (local-only = insecure)
